BNF antibacterial drug classes (BNF section 5.1)

Source: R/openprescribing.R
op_antibiotic_classes.Rd

The sub-sections of BNF chapter 5, section 1 ("Antibacterial drugs"), with the BNF codes that get_op_spending accepts. Use it to pick classes for get_op_antibiotics.

Usage

op_antibiotic_classes()

Value

A data.frame with columns number (BNF section number, e.g. "5.1.1"), code (BNF code prefix, e.g. "050101") and class. The first row is the whole of section 5.1.

Details

The classes follow the BNF's own grouping, which is by drug class or use rather than by AWaRe category, ATC group or the UKHSA/ESPAUR definitions, and some classes straddle those (for example 5.1.7 and 5.1.13 mix agents). Section 5.1.9 (antituberculosis) and 5.1.10 (antileprotic) are included for completeness but are normally excluded from community antibiotic-stewardship analyses. BNF classification is revised over time; confirm any code you rely on with search_op_bnf.

Examples

op_antibiotic_classes()
#>    number   code                                              class
#> 1     5.1   0501                            All antibacterial drugs
#> 2   5.1.1 050101                                        Penicillins
#> 3   5.1.2 050102 Cephalosporins, carbapenems and other beta-lactams
#> 4   5.1.3 050103                                      Tetracyclines
#> 5   5.1.4 050104                                    Aminoglycosides
#> 6   5.1.5 050105                                         Macrolides
#> 7   5.1.6 050106                         Clindamycin and lincomycin
#> 8   5.1.7 050107                             Some other antibiotics
#> 9   5.1.8 050108                      Sulfonamides and trimethoprim
#> 10  5.1.9 050109                             Antituberculosis drugs
#> 11 5.1.10 050110                                 Antileprotic drugs
#> 12 5.1.11 050111           Metronidazole, tinidazole and ornidazole
#> 13 5.1.12 050112                                         Quinolones
#> 14 5.1.13 050113                           Urinary-tract infections
